findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
The dish machine in the kitchen was observed to have Laundry Chlorine Bleach hooked up to it and was only heat sanitizing at 146F. The PIC called EcoLab regarding this issue. The EcoLab representative has ordered a part to repair the dish machine, as it is not properly reaching a heat sanitizing temperature of 165F or above. The Laundry Chlorine Bleach was disconnected from the machine, as this was the wrong chemical delivered by US Foods. The EcoLab representative explained that the dish machine does not always properly reach the heat sanitizing temperature needed due to heavy usage and not having a booster directly on the machine, therefore, there is an ultra-sanitizer chemical hooked up to the machine to ensure that it is sanitizing dishes. The PIC will be obtaining this chemical to ensure that it is sanitizing. Ensure that this dish machine is not used until this chemical is obtained and is properly sanitizing at the label-recommended concentration. 

The Chlorine sanitizing dish machine in the bar area is observed to have an “Out of Order” sign on it and a part has been ordered for it. The facility has been bringing the bar dishes to the kitchen to be cleaned. 

A follow up is scheduled on 12/8/2025 to ensure that the kitchen dish machine has been repaired and is properly sanitizing. A spot check will be conducted when the bar dish machine has been repaired to ensure that it is properly sanitizing.

findings.comment:

1. Red onions with a date of 11/20. All pickled items made in-house should be discarded after 7 days. 
2. Two containers of cooked and cooled cauliflower with a date of 11/22. 
3. A pan of mashed potatoes with a date of 11/26. 

CORRECTED- All items were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Ensure that all Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods are date-marked, with day 1 being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded by the end of day 7.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee in the coffee bar was observed to don gloves without washing their hands before engaging in food preparation. CORRECTED- Discussed this with the PIC and the employee was educated on the importance of handwashing before donning gloves. Ensure that food employees are properly washing their hands before engaging in food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink in the coffee bar was observed to be used as a dump sink and to wash dishes in. Handwashing sinks can ONLY be used for the intended purpose of handwashing. Dishes need to be brought to the dish area in the kitchen to be washed. Dishes cannot properly be washed, rinsed, and sanitized in only a handwashing sink. Handwashing sinks cannot be used for a dump sink either. It is highly recommended to add a dump sink in the coffee bar. CORRECTED- The employees were educated to use a bucket to dump into and to take the dishes back to the dish area. This will be spot checked at the next routine inspection (at least 90 days).
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There is no signage indicating which sink is the handwashing sink in the bar. There is soap and napkins at one sink that is likely the handwashing sink. This sink also has a strainer in it which allows for dumping. CORRECTED- The facility was given handwashing signage to place at this sink and was instructed to remove the strainer. Ensure that handwashing sinks are ONLY used for the intended purpose of handwashing and always have a sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands at that handwashing sink. This will be spot checked at the next routine inspection to ensure that this was done (at least 90 days).
findings.citation_text: 6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The Coca Cola two door cooler was observed to be at an ambient temperature of 50F during the inspection. All items, except for small containers of shelf stable creamer, a package of blueberry muffins, and a package of danishes, were probed and probed to be between 46F and 52F. CORRECTED- Multiple items, including two containers of thousand island dressing, containers of vinaigrette, and a container of ranch, were all voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Ensure that TCS food is maintained at 41F or less. 

The yogurt display cooler in the buffet area had an ambient temperature of 51F. Containers of yogurt were probed to be between 49F and 54F. The yogurts were voluntarily discarded. Ensure that TCS food is held at 41F or less. 

The yogurt display cooler in the coffee bar had an ambient temperature of 53F. A container of fruit was probed to be at 47F. The containers of fruit and yogurt in this display cooler were all discarded. Ensure that TCS food is held at 41F or less. 

(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: FIRST REPEAT- There was a gallon of milk observed to not have any date marking on it. CORRECTED- The PIC was unsure of when the milk was opened and the milk was voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Ensure that all TCS food prepared and held in an establishment for more than 24 hours is marked with the date of preparation or opening and is discarded on the end of the 7th day. 

 (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: The two door Coca Cola cooler was observed to be holding TCS foods at temperatures between 46F and 52F. These items were discarded. Ensure that this cooler is serviced and repaired to allow TCS foods to be held at under 41F. A follow up will be conducted on 9/23/2024 to ensure that this cooler has been repaired and is functioning properly. 

The yogurt display cooler in the buffet area was holding yogurts at temperatures between 49F and 54F. The yogurts were voluntarily discarded. Ensure that this cooler is repaired and is functioning properly to allow TCS food to be held at under 41F. A follow up will be conducted on 9/23/2024 to ensure that this cooler has been repaired and is functioning properly. 

The yogurt display cooler in the coffee bar had an ambient temperature of 53F. The containers of fruit and yogurt inside were voluntarily discarded. The left side of the cooler is holding at an ambient temperature of 60F. None of the items on this side are required to be refrigerated at 41F or below. Ensure that this cooler is repaired to allow TCS food to be held at 41F or under. A follow up will be conducted on 9/23/2024 to ensure that this cooler has been repaired and is properly maintaining TCS foods at 41F or below. 

EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The low door cooler in the kitchen is still out of temperature (liquid egg temperature of 47F) and contained some food items.  Discard the food and place a “Do not use” sign on the door to prevent food storage until fixed and working properly.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Violation #1 is out of compliance based on the number of priority and priority foundation violations found during the routine inspection.

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Multiple food items were observed to be stored in the line cooler uncovered or in opened packages.  Discussed with PIC, who discarded the food.  Ensure food is covered during storage to prevent cross contamination.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The two ice machines and the ice bin on the server was observed to contain mold/residue.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure ice machines are cleaned regularly to prevent mold growth and ice contamination.

4-602.11: (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
A low door cooler in the kitchen was observed to not be working properly.  The cooler had an ambient temperature of 47-49F, and an unopened container of sour cream was found to have a temperature of 49F(probe).  All items in the cooler were discarded expect for a couple jugs of BBQ sauce.  Ensure the temperatures of coolers are taken regularly help recognize when there is equipment failure.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Multiple containers were observed in different coolers throughout the kitchen to not be date marked, or held past the maximum 7 day holding time.  Discussed with PIC and a kitchen employee, all items were discarded.  Ensure all food containers are date marked if held longer than 24 hours and discarded after 7 days.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Spoons in the prep cooler were observed to be stored in the sauce to serve with the handles almost completely submerged in the sauce.  Discussed with PIC, COS.  Ensure in use utensils are stored with the handles not in contact with the food.

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
The walk-in freezer has an accumulation of ice in the back.  Discussed with PIC, who stated it gets cleaned regularly.  Ensure the walk-in freezer is serviced and working properly to prevent any future refrigeration issues.

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Areas in need of maintenance:
1.  The wall holding the hand sink by the kitchen “out” door is missing paint and is bare (caulk/seal).
2.  Holes in walls throughout the kitchen (by the coffee pots at the server station, around the back hand sink by the exit door (caulk/seal). 
3.  The wall holding the hand sink by the exit door is missing paint and is bare (paint/seal).
4.  The door jamb leading into the dish area has missing or broken coving tile pieces.
5.  Caulk the 3 part sink and the dish line in the dish room
6.  Hallway leading to the banquet area has missing paint exposing bare wood (paint/seal).
7.  The wall by the banquet prep sink has a hole/gap in the wall.

Ensure these areas are serviced and/or repaired to create a smooth, non-absorbent, easily cleanable surface. 
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Some mops were observed to be stored with the mop head down on the floor.  Ensure mops are stored in a way to allow the mop head to air dry properly to prevent mold and mildew growth.

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
There are currently no employees who have allergen awareness certification.  Ensure all CFPMs obtain this certification within 30 days of employment.  An allergen awareness handout is given at time of inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.
